frameworks.name: Confused Look Content Format
frameworks.description: A content format where the creator uses a facial expression or reaction of confusion to create curiosity and encourage viewers to continue watching.
frameworks.when_to_use: When a brand wants to create curiosity-driven short-form content with a strong first-second hook.
frameworks.example: A creator sees an unexpected product feature and reacts with a confused expression before revealing the explanation.

metadata.key_principle: Strong emotional reactions can create curiosity gaps that increase watch time and engagement.
metadata.article_summary: This article explains a short-form content pattern based on a confused facial reaction, showing how simple human emotions can be used as attention hooks.

content_patterns.name: Reaction-based hook
content_patterns.description: Use a recognizable human reaction before explaining the context.
content_patterns.example: Creator looks confused first, then reveals the surprising reason.
